title: Love Itself Is Shiva
hookLine: love and Shiva are two, say those who don't know: Tirumular's short verse
carry: anbe sivam: love itself is shiva
tomorrow: The King, the Merchant and the Mother
last: THE HEART IS THE REAL OFFERING.

cards: Love and Shiva are two, say those who don't know. That's the first line of a short Tamil verse, spoken by a man the tradition calls Tirumular. How he got that name is strange.
A traveling yogi comes upon a herd of cows gathered around the body of their cowherd, who has just died. The cows are lowing, circling, refusing to leave him. The yogi can't bear it.
So, the story says, he leaves his own body and enters the cowherd's. And the cowherd stands up.

teach.b: Here's the rest, as the Periya Puranam tells it, in paraphrase. The cows, comforted, go home. The yogi means to return to his own body, but when he looks for it, it's gone.
So he stays in the cowherd's body, under the cowherd's name, Mular, and settles down to meditate and compose the Tirumantiram, a long book of verses on Shiva and the path to him.
It sits in the Tirumurai, the collection that holds the Tevaram. Now the verse, in paraphrase. Love and Shiva are two, say those who don't know.
No one knows that love itself is Shiva.
When they know that love itself is Shiva, they rest there, as love, as Shiva. The verse doesn't say Shiva is loving, the way you'd say a person is kind. It goes further: the love is Shiva.
Not a quality he has, but who he is. Now go back to the field. The story starts with a man who couldn't bear the grief of some cows.
He wasn't seeking a vision. He was moved by animals crying for their herder, and gave up his own body to comfort them.

teach.h: HE DID IT BEFORE HE WROTE IT
teach.b: Before he wrote a single verse, he'd already done what the verse says.
Looking back over these Tamil days: Appar, who belonged wholly to Shiva; Sambandar, whose heart was stolen; Kannappa, who held nothing back; and Tirumular, saying it plainly.
Tamil Shaivas still write it in two words: anbe sivam, love is Shiva.

how: Tirumular is honored among the Nayanmars, the Shaiva saints of the Tamil country, and the words 'anbe sivam', love is Shiva, from his verse are spoken and written by Tamil Shaivas.

games.q: what does “tamil shaivism and the tevaram” mean?
o: Tamil Shiva devotion, in hymns like the Tevaram and Tirumantiram
a Sanskrit epic retold in Tamil by a wandering yogi
a Tamil cattle festival honoring cowherds and their herds

games.q: Tirumular and the cows — tap the pairs.
p: gone when he looked for it

s: the verse says Shiva is loving, as a person is kind
it goes further: love itself is Shiva, not a quality he has.
in the story, the yogi enters the cowherd's body to comfort the cows
the Tirumantiram has nothing to do with the Tevaram
it sits in the Tirumurai, the same sacred collection that holds the Tevaram.

games.q: you're a traveling yogi. in a field, cows are circling the body of their dead cowherd, lowing and refusing to leave. what do you do?
o: walk on; it's not your herd.
leave your own body and enter the cowherd's.
go to the village for help.
games.why: the story says he entered the cowherd's body, and the cowherd stood up and took the cows home.

practice: Bring to mind someone you love, a person or even an animal, see their face for a moment, and feel the warmth that comes with it.

Then gently let the face fade and stay with the warmth, not the person now, just the love; when the mind goes looking for the face, let it, and come back. If you pray, rest in the verse's two words, anbe sivam.
If you don't, just rest in the warmth.

wordCard.voice: Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram. Today, Tirumular, the yogi who entered a cowherd's body to comfort his cows, and whose verse says love itself is Shiva. Today's word.
